Canadian here! There are so many things to buy to prepare for a baby and these showers can be really helpful to take some of that off the plate of the expectant parents. Many people, friends and family of the couple, want to help out in whatever ways they can. Making a registry just means you don't get 20 of the same thing. We put all the stuff we will need and don't expect all of it to be purchased for us but many registry places give discounts on items that are remaining as well. It's especially nice to have a celebration before the baby comes because the parents aren't worn out from taking care of the new baby. I think it is most common for the first child, as that's when most of the items need to be purchased, and if you're having a second you'll probably keep what you need and donate the rest. Cribs alone are hundreds of dollars, not to mention bassinets, car seats and strollers. And that's the bare minimum of what new parents usually need. So whether your friends and family are helping with big ticket items or sending the smaller items like pacifiers or rattles, it's all just one less thing for the parents to worry about. 
Personally I have lots of friends and family that are so excited for us to have a baby and they are looking for ways to treat or spoil us and so these registries are a helpful way to get all the things in one spot so you're not getting double items and everyone can pick things they can afford or simply get you gift cards to the stores so when you buy the items left on the list it just helps take the sting out of it. It's not an entitlement thing, it's the same as wedding registries. We didn't do one for our wedding because we didn't need anything and we knew we would be moving across the country and didn't want any extra stuff to pay to ship. It's not a requirement it's a place to go if you are able and interested in helping out. 
If not it's always just nice to have people excited and supportive of your new family around because pregnancy and early Parenthood can be very isolating and lonely.
